title: NorthPoint Dedicated Capacity Discovery

summary: Initial discovery for Dedicated capacity: NorthPoint needs reserved GPUs for production LLM infra, strict isolation and audit requirements, and a burst strategy to handle monthly statement generation peaks. Team is interested in a pilot for benchmarking latency and throughput on a 16x A100 equivalent pool.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-29 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE backup), Marcus Hale (Head of ML Ops, NorthPoint), Sasha Kim (VP Eng), Eli Rivers (Platform SRE), Tina Park (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood. Quick roll call, you all there?
[00:05] Marcus: Yep, Marcus here.
[00:06] Sasha: Sasha, hi.
[00:08] Eli: Eli on my side.
[00:10] Tina: Tina here.
[00:12] Jordan: Awesome. So goal for today is to understand NorthPoint's needs around dedicated capacity 
— reserved GPUs, isolation, burst strategy, scaling expectations 
— and see if Dedicated or Private makes more sense. Priya will do the technical deep dive.
[00:25] Priya: Hi all. To start, can you share current stack and what you're running now?
[00:32] Marcus: Sure. Right now we've got a mix. For research and low-priority workloads we use hosted APIs 
— some OpenAI and internal models on EKS. Production customer-facing flows (chat, statement summarization) are on self-hosted infra with Kubernetes, using 8x A100-ish nodes but it's a bit of a patchwork. Our primary concerns are isolation / data residency and predictable latency during month-end runs.
[00:50] Priya: Got it. When you say month-end runs, what's the spike pattern and peak concurrency?
[00:55] Marcus: We do a daily summary for users but the big spike is monthly statement generation for 1.2M customers. It's batched 
— not all at once 
— but over a 2
–3 hour window we see token throughput jump 6x. Memory/KV cache and prefix reuse help but right now we lose latency SLOs and rack up costs.
[01:15] Sasha: And security 
— we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, KMS integration, and audit trails for model inputs/outputs for compliance.
[01:23] Priya: Totally reasonable. Redwood Dedicated supports private VPCs and we can enable customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. We also stream audit logs and have long-term retention as an add-on. For the month-end burst, we have a few typical patterns: reserved baseline capacity + burst capacity from a shared pool, or pre-scheduled autoscaling with warm pools. Which approach were you thinking?
[01:44] Eli: We prefer reserved capacity for predictable throughput, but we need the ability to burst if the queued job backlog grows. Ideally burst should be fast 
— under ~5 minutes to spin up 
— and we need clear cost controls.
[01:55] Marco: One thing to note 
— burst to what? Public hosted? Dedicated burst? We offer a couple: dedicated-only with burst headroom reserved, or a hybrid fallback to Redwood hosted API which is faster to scale but has different isolation guarantees.
[02:10] Marcus: We can't send regulated PII to shared hosted endpoints. So hybrid fallback is only acceptable for sanitized, non-PII workloads. Burst within Dedicated with extra reserved burst nodes is preferred.
[02:21] Priya: Understood. For that we'd size baseline reserved GPUs for average load and add a burst pool 
— we can do scheduled burst windows for month-end or event-driven autoscale with pre-warmed capacity. Do you have target latency SLOs?
[02:35] Sasha: For interactive flows we need sub-500ms token latency for customer chat. For batch statement generation, throughput matters more 
— we target finishing the job within the 2
–3 hour window with p99 latency under X for critical steps.
[02:50] Tina: We also are evaluating model variants 
— larger LLMs for higher-quality summaries and smaller quantized models for cheap, fast passes. We'd like Redwood to support quantized execution and recommendations.
[03:02] Priya: We support quantized variants and can recommend profiles. We also do per-model performance profiles so we can estimate tokens/sec on the hardware. Typical throughput on 8x A100-equivalent pool for a 7B quantized model is ~xxk tokens/sec 
— we'll send a sizing worksheet.
[03:18] Marcus: That worksheet will be helpful. A couple compliance questions: can you support private control plane / air-gapped? And what about SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[03:28] Jordan: We have Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem options) that offers customer-managed control plane and optional air-gapped deployments. For most customers Dedicated with VPC peering plus customer-managed KMS and SAML works. We can share our SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[03:41] Eli: On networking, we need to peer to our VPC and limit egress. Also need details on port lists and firewall rules.
[03:48] Priya: We'll share a network diagram and required ports. For Dedicated we typically do VPC peering or PrivateLink; in Private/on-prem we can do more strict isolation but it's a heavier lift.
[03:59] Sasha: What about multi-tenant risk? Even with VPC peering, do GPUs share tenancy? We need assurance that other tenants won't access our KV cache or model artifacts.
[04:10] Priya: In Dedicated we dedicate GPU hosts to your capacity; you get tenant isolation at the host level. There's still a shared control plane unless you choose Private. KV caches and model artifacts can be isolated 
— we can keep caches on your hosts or encrypted storage.
[04:23] Marcus: Great. Can you walk through typical autoscaling policies? We want predictable scaling without noisy neighbor issues.
[04:30] Priya: Sure. We generally recommend: 1) baseline reserved capacity sized to handle 70
–80% of expected peak; 2) warm standby nodes (burst pool) scheduled for predictable windows; 3) event-driven autoscale with pre-warm and cooldowns for unexpected spikes. We apply balanced scheduling to avoid a single tenant hogging GPU scheduler.
[04:50] Eli: How quick are kernel compile/initialization times when spinning up new nodes? For some models cold start can be minutes.
[04:57] Marco: Model load time depends on model size and quantization. For a 70B model it's longer; for quantized 7B variants it's sub-minute with our optimized runtime. We also support warm model preloads to reduce cold starts 
— that's what warm pools are for.
[05:12] Marcus: On monitoring and observability, we need per-route latency, token counts, audit logs, and per-model dashboards. Also cost breakdown per token and per route is critical for our chargeback model.
[05:23] Jordan: Redwood Console exposes per-token cost, latency breakdown, and tracing hooks. We can also stream metrics to your Prometheus / Grafana.
[05:31] Tina: For the pilot, we'd want to run our summary workload and see p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec, plus cost estimates.
[05:38] Priya: Sounds good. We'll provide a test harness that can replay your workload or we can run synthetic tests with your prompt set.
[05:45] Sasha: Timeline 
— we're aiming to onboard a production-grade solution before next quarter for the statement generation. We have procurement constraints and need SSO and SOC2 artifacts to move forward quickly.
[05:56] Jordan: Typical timeline: pilot (2 weeks of bench testing) -> procurement/security review -> pilot expansion -> GA rollout. We can align with your quarter.
[06:05] Marcus: Pricing question 
— how do you price burst capacity? Is burst billed at on-demand rates?
[06:10] Jordan: Baseline reserved capacity is committed (monthly), burst capacity is billed at a higher short-term rate. We can also do committed burst headroom at a discounted rate if you want predictable costs. We'll include pricing scenarios in the deck.
[06:22] Eli: One more technical 
— can we pin model versions and ensure rollbacks / canary deploys? We need deterministic rollouts for regulatory reasons.
[06:30] Priya: Yes, rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback policies are supported. You can pin model versions per route and define automatic fallback to a quantized variant if latency breaches SLO.
[06:41] Marcus: Any concerns about data residency? Our legal team requires logs to remain in-region for EU customers.
[06:46] Jordan: We provide region control for Dedicated and Private; logs and persistent storage can be region-restricted. We'll note that in the security packet.
[06:55] Sasha: Ok, can you summarize the immediate next steps?
[06:59] Jordan: Sure. We'll: 1) send Dedicated pricing deck and GPU sizing worksheet, 2) share SOC2, network diagram and required ports, 3) propose pilot dates and provide the test harness, 4) recommend baseline and burst node sizing options. Does that cover it?
[07:15] Marcus: Yes. Also can you include a sample SLA and an example canary rollout plan?
[07:20] Jordan: Yep will include sample SLA and canary plan.
[07:23] Tina: Quick Q 
— any recommended quantization tradeoffs for our summary model? We care about fidelity for financial language.
[07:29] Priya: For financial text, we usually recommend int8 quantization for 7B-ish models; that preserves fidelity better than aggressive 4-bit modes. We'll include model-specific recommendations based on your prompt set.
[07:41] Sasha: Are we able to do a direct benchmark on our dataset or do you need sanitized sample?
[07:46] Priya: We can do either: you can run the harness in your environment against Dedicated or we can run synthetic with redacted samples. For PII, we'll prioritize on-prem or VPC-peered test runs.
[07:58] Marcus: Great. Any blockers from your side?
[08:01] Jordan: None from Redwood. We'll follow up with the docs and proposed pilot window.
[08:06] Eli: For networking we'll gather firewall info and send it to Jordan.
[08:10] Jordan: Awesome. We'll also include expected lead times for provisioning reserved GPUs 
— typically 2
–3 weeks from contract sign if we need custom host assignment, quicker if inventory available.
[08:22] Sasha: Perfect. Let's aim for a pilot start in three weeks.
[08:25] Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. We'll send notes and next-steps after this call.

[08:35] ��������— meeting ends �

Recap (explicit):
- Redwood to send Dedicated pricing deck, GPU sizing worksheet, SOC2 and network diagram
- Schedule two-week pilot benchmark (NorthPoint to confirm dates)

End.
